profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at IBM
profile.summary:
I'm a software engineer that writes both application and system-level code.  I've coded in a variety of languages, both compiled and interpreted.  I like working with Linux, and have been using it for over 20 years.  I'm also familiar with AIX, and have been known to dabble in Windows development.  I'm a fan of open-source software, and have run a variety of Linux distributions over the years.

I'm an expert C developer, and proficient in Java as well.  I'm quite comfortable with shell scripting, and have written a few Perl utilities when heavy lifting was required.  I'm comfortable with CVS and Subversion, and have designed and implemented automated build systems for various projects.  I've been known to build installation packages as well, using both RPM and MSI.

I've worked with IBM mainframes for much of my career, and as such have experience with Linux on System z, z/OS, UNIX System Services, and System z firmware.

I have ported numerous open-source utilities to z/OS, in an effort to improve the usability and functionality of the system.  Some of these became supported products, like PHP and bzip2.  Others are available on a unsupported basis, like Info-Zip and less.

positions.title: Advisory Software Engineer
positions.description:
Designed, created, and executed test infrastructure for IBM z/OS Container Extensions (zCX). 

Designed, implemented, and tested IBM ZHPM for z/VM.  Created development, build, and deployment infrastructure.  Worked with clients during beta program to implement feedback.

Designed and implemented code for IBM KVM on z Systems.  Setup build environment and refactored existing product code.  Developed automated unit test strategy.

Ran weekly "Lunch & Learn"​ sessions for an audience of 75+ people.  

Organized and hosted multiple Reddit "Ask Me Anything" sessions for a variety of z Systems topics

Worked with customer account team to resolve technical hurdles and get a solution into production.

Authored an article in the "z/OS Hot Topics" magazine on zHPM for IBM KVM for z Systems.

Presented zHPM on zKVM to the Metropolitan VM User's Group

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.description:
Designed and implemented code for zEnterprise Unified Resource Manager.  Wrote Java non-blocking IO networking stack for inter-component communication.  Took ownership of the Guest Platform Management Provider (GPMP) component, while implementing new features and fixing bugs.  Rewrote CPU data collection code, using JNI to bridge to Linux kernel taskstats interface.  Integrated GPMP into existing firmware build processes.  Assisted in porting GPMP to Windows platform, including writing Installshield installer.  Wrote code-signing toolchain to sign executables, libraries, and device drivers.  

Participated in a "Biztech" project that evaluated candidates for a Mobile Desktop Virtualization solution.  Tested and explored multiple USB ARM stick solutions, and prepared feasibility study for potential adoption by CIO.

Developed infrastructure for z/OS Management Facility.  Wrote code in PL/X to work with system dumps.  Implemented C APIs for said code.  Updated build system to use modern compiler options.  Improved API performance by using compiled SYSREXX code.

Transferred the z/OS Health Checker component to Rochester.  Wrote and shipped sample health checks in Metal C.

Led the Ported Tools team in porting opens-source applications to z/OS UNIX.  Applications included PHP, bzip2, and cURL.  The team was based out of Shanghai, China.  Chaired all team meetings and communicated status to upline management.  Created and maintained software build and version control systems.  Ported other software to z/OS in spare time.
